blocks.value: Telling these apart will save you more time than anything else in this lesson.
Syntax errors: the compiler catches them

**Syntax errors** are invalid statements that the compiler encounters. When it hits one, it produces one or more error messages, and **no program is produced at all**. To debug, locate and correct the grammatical mistake.
The compiler tells you the file, the line, and often points at the exact column. Fix the grammar and recompile.
Logical errors: only you catch them
If the program compiles with no syntax errors, it is ready to execute. But if it produces **incorrect results**, that is a **logical error**.
Nothing is grammatically wrong, so Java says nothing. These are harder to find and resolve because there is no error message, the programmer must locate and correct them.
the program will not build. **Logical error:** the program builds and lies to you.
